content.collection_notes:
# Christminster

Story Z5 R4/961117. Local R4/961117 matches the archive story and game/guide IFDB identity. Audrey De Lisle guide was revised 1995-12-20 and names two proofplayers. It does not declare one exact target release/serial; a comment refers to version 1, and other comments warn that names and final key metal may vary. Preserve older-guide/later-release uncertainty.

Complete the college investigation, book/clue gathering, elixir and dinner phases, then carry the rescue through the crypt and stairs to Malcolm's final escape north. Require the genuine concluding rescue narrative. A witnessed murder, temporary revival, dinner transition or 50-point annotation is not by itself completion.

The guide groups work by area and includes variable names, keys and timing rather than a fully fixed transcript. Do not type blank placeholders or blindly substitute its example scholar names. Keep ingredients separate until the proper recipe step. Verify a checkpoint before the tightly timed crypt endgame; avoid synthetic probes during that sequence.

Use only small broker help excerpts (at most 9 lines / 1000 characters). No complete guide reads, direct guide URL access or serial excerpts to reconstruct a guide. Help is suggested, not observed game evidence. Resolve startup questions/key pauses first. Make an early safe checkpoint and milestone saves only at confirmed ordinary command prompts, and verify actual success. Menu Enter is an empty command, not literal space or the word RETURN; other keys only as requested on screen. On timeout use await_output only: no flush commands, keys, repeated inputs, new SAVE or waits sent to the game. Collect useful varied labeled synthetic probes and real same-intent repairs with event IDs, not quotas or repeated filler. Use one command at a time near hazards/questions/menus. Keep ordinary deaths and failures labeled as failures. Parent independently checks actual concluding narrative in raw output. No training, evaluation or publication.
content.checkpoint_policy: Early safe checkpoint and milestone saves only at confirmed ordinary command prompts; verify actual success. Resolve questions/key pauses first. Never save to flush a timeout.

# Christminster progress (branch b9) — *** GAME WON *** 48/50, 675 turns.

Location: WON. Final: Top of Secret Staircase -> pull Malcolm north (e01139) -> rescue + hospital epilogue + "*** You have won ***".
Result: Score 48/50 (missing 2 optional: likely wistaria-roof climb + manhole-down/book point — guide numbering differs; win banner explicit). Moves 675.
Winning path (b9): before-crypt-45 restore -> E crypt (655, 10:30) -> 7 waits (murders) -> dagger (663) -> search Bungay SILVER key (664) -> cut noose +1=46 (665) -> pull E (666) -> take retort (667) -> pour elixir +1=47 Malcolm alive (668) -> HIDE key in bag + close (669-670) -> pull up (671, Jarboe demands KNIFE not key) -> kill-with-dagger makes Jarboe FLEE down into fire (672) -> open bag (673) -> unlock silver (674) -> open door (675) -> pull Malcolm north WINS (676th move... recorded 675 turns).
KEY SOLUTION: silver key MUST be hidden in closed handbag at top; visible key = begging stalemate (wrist loop, unlock blocked, give = trap). Hidden key = Jarboe demands knife, one slash routs him into the crypt fire (charred bones in epilogue).
Deaths (labeled failures): b7 e01090 fire collapse 678 (push mocked); b8 e01113 fire 675 (give-key trap + recon).
Annotated: 36 total (6 seg4: snail-pour-syn, snail-flip, snail-cut-omit, snail-synonym, decanter-port-take, decanter-hand). No crypt probes (timed) — correct.
Checkpoints: before-crypt-45 (used x2, both verified); dinner-done-44; elixir-done-41; others.
Evidence: e01139 (b9) contains full concluding rescue narrative + win banner + 48/50. Finish submitted with e01139.

events.intent: Press key to begin game past title screen
events.response:
You haven't seen your brother Malcolm since he received his fellowship at 
Biblioll College - pressure of work was his excuse not to come down to London. 
So when you received that telegram from him you leapt at the excuse to come up 
to the university town of Christminster for the day and visit him.

CHRISTMINSTER
An Interactive Conspiracy by Gareth Rees.

Please type "help licence" for details about the absence of warranty and about 
how you may distribute "Christminster". Type "help" for instructions.
Release 4 / Serial number 961117 / Inform v1502 Library 5/12
Standard interpreter 1.1

Chapel Street
It is a hot summer's day in Christminster, the kind of day that makes you think 
of strawberries and cream and punting on the river. The morning sunlight beams 
down on the cobbles and on the great wooden gate of Biblioll College to the 
east.

The gate is closed.

events.intent: Learn the keyword cipher method from Zinovic
events.response:
A keyword substitution cipher is obtained by choosing a fairly lengthy word or 
name with no repeated letters, for example "Gwyneth", and using G to code for 
A, W for B and so on. When the letters of the name are used up, use the 
remaining letters in alphabetical order. The cipher obtained by using "Gwyneth" 
is this:

 Plaintext: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
Ciphertext: GWYNETHABCDFIJKLMOPQRSUVXZ

To decode a keyword cipher, you will need to guess the word the coder has 
chosen, or else use the methods for decrypting random ciphers.

events.intent: Inspect the Introitus Apertus book
events.response:
The book, by Eugenius Philalethes and dated 1662, is a long treatise on alchemy 
(the art of turning base metals into gold and silver by the action of a 
mysterious substance called the "Philosopher's Stone") and how the author 
intends to produce vast quantities of gold and destroy the evil system of 
money, so that "this prop and stay of the anti-Christ may come to naught".

The bulk of the text is a long series of recipes, in which strange allegorical 
names like "Philosophic Mercury", "the Dew of Hermes" and so on substitute for 
real chemicals.

Near the end of the book you discover the following passage:

"At the close of three years labour, performed with diligence, patience and 
good will, you will have a small quantity of a reddish powder, of a splendid 
vermillion, a deeper and fuller hue than cinnabar. Glorify God and be thankful!

"To form the Virgin's Milk, which is the cause of prophetic dreams and mystic 
visions, dissolve the powder in a bottle of good wine, which you may give to 
your cellarer to put away so that it may mature in darkness over a space of at 
least five years.

"Afterwards, uncork the bottle carefully, and treat the Milk by the recipe 
described elsewhere, to possess the Elixir of Life. It is possible to further 
transform the Elixir into the Powder of Projection, but I will say no more 
herein."

What a load of nonsense!
